title: The Loyalty Tax
hook: Your loyalty to your company is actually a financial penalty.
script:
(Visual: Split screen. Left side shows a dedicated employee staying 5 years. Right side shows a "job hopper" switching every 2 years.)

Narrator: In the corporate world, there is a hidden tax called the Loyalty Tax. 

Most professionals believe that staying at one company for years builds "equity" and "trust" that leads to big promotions. 

But look at the math. 

Internal raises usually hover around 3-8%. Market corrections—when you switch companies—often jump 20% to 50%. 

By staying "loyal" for five years, you aren't proving your value; you are subsidizing your employer's payroll. 

The company isn't rewarding your loyalty; they are benefiting from your hesitation to check your market value. 

In a capitalist labor market, the only way to get a market-rate salary is to actually enter the market.

Stop treating your job like a marriage and start treating it like a contract.
caption:
The most expensive mistake Indian professionals make is confusing professional stability with financial growth. Your "loyalty" is often just a discount you're giving your boss. 📉
